en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
Sakkaccavagga 33.
The Training Rule on Successive Order.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were eating almsfood by picking and choosing here and there... [as before] ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I shall eat almsfood in regular order.
Almsfood is to be eaten in regular order."
Whoever, out of disrespect, eats almsfood while making disparaging remarks here and there, commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
For one who is lacking mindfulness,
for one who is unaware,
and for one who is ill.
He disparages others when giving;
he disparages another when pouring into their bowl;
regarding the subsequent meal.
In times of distress,
for one who is insane,
and for the first offender.
The third training rule is concluded.
